      "observations": [
        "All 1,357 lines of the exact owned diff and all 38 changed-path metadata entries were read. The change replaces flat path exports with segment modules, adds the handwritten ModuleHierarchy implementation, updates seven actual Graph operation consumers and pagination tests, moves generated path files, and removes the unexported generated SendMailRequestBody file. This is functional generator/integration work, not a bulk generated-only exclusion.",
        "generate_paths builds a sorted set of supported API path nodes, writes root exports, emits supported path modules with operations plus child declarations, then writes export-only files for unsupported ancestors. ModuleHierarchy walks every leaf toward the root and deduplicates/sorts child names with BTreeSet; concrete modules keep their own operations instead of being overwritten as intermediate-only exports.",
        "generate_types uses the same hierarchy but separately records direct schema modules and namespaces. The writer combines direct and child exports, skips empty exports and creates necessary parent directories before writing. The owned code used SUPPORTED_TYPES; accepted code separately selects SUPPORTED_OBJECTS and SUPPORTED_ENUMS, so later schema-generation behavior is not projected back.",
        "ModuleName keeps a plain snake-case file segment and creates a Rust identifier separately. move therefore lives in move.rs but is exported and consumed as r#move. raw_snakeify handles punctuation and case; snakeify applies r# to keyword names. base_name now strips only one leading microsoft.graph. prefix and borrows the remaining string, rather than replacing all occurrences. The tested move case does not prove every keyword or arbitrary input is valid.",
        "PathModule wraps the extracted API Path and its child modules, emits pub mod declarations, then emits operations sorted by method. Generated path modules now export their children. Seven handwritten clients use the nested paths for folder creation, draft creation/update, fetch, move, send, folder deltas and message deltas; the changed constructor arguments, await and response/listener calls stay in their existing order in the owned hunks.",
        "The fixed accepted ModuleHierarchy file has the exact owned blob 389f735a0841a44241a4f968ecfa194b20edea15. Current generate_paths and raw-name separation retain this architecture; current move_message_request uses r#move::Post and the generated request still constructs /me/messages/{message_id}/move. Later optional typed request-body fields, base_api_url and additional copy exports are separate accepted-source phases.",
        "The four new ModuleHierarchy tests directly assert slash/function-segment sanitation, move.rs versus r#move, top-level/nested schema paths, and sorted combined direct/child exports. All 12 new assertions omit expected-behavior messages. The changed oxidize test wraps Path in PathModule but retains a message-less negative Put body-lifetime assertion. Pagination tests change request type paths while their parsed response and next/delta link assertions stay unchanged. No tests were run.",
        "The six R100 generated moves retain their old operation blobs at the owned landing. Other moved generated files add child pub mod lines. The deleted SendMailRequestBody file has no matching reference/export in the owned rust/ms_graph_tb and graph_xpcom scope; absence in that exact scope is not a global unused-code proof.",
        "Handwritten hierarchy comments distinguish file names, Rust identifiers, namespaces and root behavior; generated comments are output disclosures, not general naming rules. The nested fold/while in build_child_modules walks ancestors and could use a short adjacent reason comment; this is a readability suggestion, not a diagnosed defect. The scoped new_without_default allowance applies to generated path modules, not all Rust code.",
        "Required primary and own review are complete retained originals. The author reports that CI does not run ms_graph_tb_extract and that almost all Try orange was known; CI/task logs were not inspected. Earlier rustfmt defects precede later remote completions and approval. Those reports do not establish fresh compile, generator-output or HTTP correctness.",
        "The complete required Parent primary2022671 and Source A own D291869 originals were read and reconciled. The primary requests nested URI-segment modules; exact owned generator, generated exports and actual clients adopt this shape.",
        "D291869 has no actual inline bodies or summary history. Author raw-identifier support is supported narrowly by move.rs/r#move source and direct tests, not a universal identifier claim. The claim that nearly all Try orange was known and ms_graph_tb_extract does not run in CI stays attributed; no CI jobs or tests were executed. Earlier rustfmt errors, later remote completions, approval and landing remain historical.",
        "The handwritten generator owns naming/layout policy for its generated files; generated disclosure comments do not establish a general source-style rule. No change was made to the generator, fixtures or deliberate guidance during this study."
